title: The board printed 'available: (empty)' for about a day while 21 ready items sat behind a lane guard whose three of four owners were dead
what_happened: monitor/board.py's candidates() carried `if not lane and m.get("lane"): continue` -- a guard written so a generic worker could not strip a live researcher's queue. Every ready item carries a lane, so the no-lane query dropped all of them and cmd_list() printed `available: (empty)`. The supply was 21 items; three of the four lane owners (RES-1/RES-2/RES-4) were no longer beating. The monitor spawned three workers to test supply, they found nothing to claim and said so precisely, and they were right: 'I had been measuring the guard, not the supply.'
why_it_was_invisible: An empty list is a well-formed answer. The guard never errored, and the reserved queue was not printed at all, so the one number that would have separated 'no work exists' from 'all work is reserved to corpses' was the number the listing suppressed.
detected_by: generic workers W-131 and W-1621, who reported the board empty while counting items themselves; the monitor then re-derived the cause
detection_latency: about one day
fix: LANE_OWNER + STALE_MIN=45 + heartbeat_age()/stale_lanes(); the guard becomes `if not lane and m.get("lane") and m["lane"] not in stale`, and the listing prints a `=== reserved ===` section instead of hiding it.

title: The quota breaker's bare-word signature also matched the string 'quota.py', so every worker that ran the check manufactured its own evidence
what_happened: quota detection matched bare words in scanned text. Those words also occur in the literal string `quota.py` and in prose about the breaker, so a worker scanning a log that merely mentioned the file -- including a sentence that DENIES a session limit -- tripped a hold. quota_state.json still carries the clearing entry `{"at": "2026-07-28T21:26:55Z", "from": "monitor-false-positive-clear"}`. Four tests had been failing on this since the day the detector was added.
why_it_was_invisible: The detector fires on its own name, so any diagnostic activity about the breaker is indistinguishable from a real outage. And a hold is a plausible state -- nothing about it looks like a bug from outside.
detected_by: the monitor, while tracing why the fleet was held
detection_latency: one day (the four failing tests dated to the detector's introduction)
fix: Detection now requires a hard signature, skips prose, and is consulted only to OPEN a hold, never to extend one.

title: A log line that trips the quota hold stays inside the scan window, so the hold could never expire -- the auto-exit was welded shut
what_happened: The breaker re-scans a rolling window of logs. The very line that opens a hold remains inside that window on the next pass, so each pass re-opens the hold it was meant to close. This is a fourth, independent gap in the same breaker, on top of the three F-21 recorded and the F-22 exit-spends-the-quota defect.
why_it_was_invisible: Each individual pass is correct: it sees a session-limit line and holds. The latch is a property of the composition of the window with the write, not of any one step.
detected_by: the monitor, in the same pass that found F-98
detection_latency: unknown -- present since the window scan was added
fix: The scan may only OPEN a hold; expiry is driven by the reset window, not by re-scanning. Verified in the wild the same night -- see C-44.

title: Eight branches were flagged 'verify gate red' for hours and none of them was red: the bash on PATH was WSL's, a different Linux with no python, and it ate the backslashes of the Windows path
what_happened: monitor/gates.py ran `["bash", path]`. The bash resolved from PATH is WSL's -- a different operating system with no python installed -- and the Windows path handed to it had its backslashes consumed as escapes. Every gate invocation failed for reasons belonging to the harness, and the merge queue recorded them as `verify gate red in <territory>`. Eight branches were held out of master on that verdict; the monitor's own gate had never been green since it was written.
why_it_was_invisible: A gate that cannot run and a gate that fails produce the same exit code. The queue's flag text names the territory, which points the reader at the branch's code rather than at the runner.
detected_by: W-1620, who traced eight branches to a single backslash
detection_latency: hours (the queue was stalled about four)
fix: Gates now resolve Git Bash explicitly (GIT_BASH_CANDIDATES, not PATH) with UTF-8 forced. Eight false reds became zero; verify:monitor, verify:arc-recon, verify:fuzzlab and pytest:engine-rig all ran and passed inside real merges within the hour.

title: With UTF-8 forced, tasklist's GBK output killed a reader thread -- and a thread's death does not propagate, it only makes stdout None, which the caller read as data
what_happened: The last link in the false-red chain. Once the gate runner forced UTF-8, the Windows `tasklist` output (GBK on this machine) raised inside the stdout reader thread. The thread died; nothing propagated; `stdout` came back as None; the caller consumed None as if it were the command's output. The commit also records that fixing only the reported backslash defect would have bought a different false red rather than a green.
why_it_was_invisible: A dead reader thread has no exit code and no exception at the call site. `None` is a value, and a caller that does not distinguish 'no output' from 'empty output' cannot tell that the measurement never happened.
detected_by: the monitor, while chasing the last false red
detection_latency: same session
fix: Fixed as part of the Git Bash + UTF-8 runner rework. Same family as F-96 and the day-1 'a tool's failure wearing the costume of a verdict' pattern.

title: The 31-line fix that ended a four-hour merge stoppage existed only in one machine's working tree for 34 minutes, and the auditor had twice stashed it without knowing
what_happened: Local reflex and ci_merge execute the working tree, not HEAD. So the Git Bash / backslash / interpreter fix in monitor/gates.py took effect and thawed the queue while HEAD's monitor/gates.py still read `return ["bash", path]`. The thaw was real but unreproducible: anyone cloning master got the broken gate. s14-gates-for-all, the branch meant to land exactly this, was still flagged red and would later collide with the uncommitted edit. The auditing session disclosed that it had run `git pull --rebase --autostash` twice over that path -- 'it restored cleanly, but I did not know I was moving the only copy of a critical fix, and that was luck rather than care.'
why_it_was_invisible: No panel reads the working tree. The dashboard, the merge log and the board all describe committed state, while the automation that produces the merge log runs uncommitted code. The difference between a dead queue and a thawing one appeared on no instrument.
detected_by: OPS-A, audit cycle 22
detection_latency: 34 minutes
fix: Committed in 99d1d5d (the audit commit itself swept it in). The proposed durable fix -- a probe that reports any monitor/*.py modified-but-uncommitted past N minutes -- is not built. New class because nothing in the vocabulary covers 'production behaviour comes from an uncommitted edit'; half_landed_change is about a change that landed partially, this one did not land at all yet ran everything.

title: Six run directories are dated in the future, up to 18.7 hours, and two MANIFEST.json utc fields copied the fabricated value
what_happened: Of 55 run directories carrying a UTC stamp, 6 are stamped ahead of real time: verify-lab/runs/20260729T180000Z-V17 (+18.7h), .../20260729T120000Z-V15 (+12.7h), theoria-arm/runs/20260729T080000Z-E14 (+8.7h), engine-rig/runs/20260729T080000Z-C11 (+8.7h), verify-lab/runs/20260729T041500Z-V14 (+4.9h), engine-rig/runs/20260729T000000Z-E11 (+0.7h), against a real 2026-07-28T23:19:46Z. The MANIFEST.json `utc` field -- one of the four required provenance fields -- copied the same value in at least the V15 and V17 cases. The shape gives it away: 180000Z / 120000Z / 080000Z / 000000Z are all on the hour, while the other 49 directories carry ragged seconds, so these were written rather than read off a clock.
why_it_was_invisible: A stamp is only checkable against an external clock, and nothing in the provenance canon compared it to one. The audit had previously downgraded nine missing-utc manifests on the reasoning that base_commit is the stronger anchor -- that reasoning inverts here, because a wrong anchor is worse than a missing one: it looks usable.
detected_by: OPS-A, audit cycle 24, with a purpose-written scanner over runs/ directory names
detection_latency: first checkable only after the six branches landed at 22:53-23:00Z; reported at 23:20Z

title: Hand-written UTC drifts forward everywhere it is hand-written, and board.py's new staleness check had to route around it by reading file mtime
what_happened: The same fabrication runs through every self-reported clock, not just run directories. monitor/ops-status/RES-3.json declares utc 2026-07-29T11:55:00Z, roughly twelve hours ahead of a file written at 23:33Z. Both PARTNER_SYNC paragraphs appended in this window are stamped ahead of their commits: b459016 (committed 21:51Z) carries 2026-07-29T10:00:00Z, 399f6d9 (committed 22:59Z) carries 2026-07-29T11:25:00Z. Inbox filenames do it too. The concrete consequence is architectural: monitor/board.py's new heartbeat_age() deliberately uses file mtime rather than the agent-written `utc` field, with an in-code note that the self-reported stamps all drift forward.
why_it_was_invisible: Every consumer that needed a time had one available, and the value was well-formed. Only a comparison against an independent clock -- or against the file's own mtime -- exposes it, and until board.py nothing made that comparison.
detected_by: the monitor (forced to work around it in board.py) and OPS-A (audit cycle 24)
detection_latency: recurrence of the day-1 finding; still open
fix: Worked around, not fixed. The day-1 harvest already recorded the heartbeat-clock version of this (data/README.md, open problem 1); it has now reached provenance manifests and the append-only status board.

title: Six delivered branches sat all night behind an absent referee, needing no code -- only a ruling on who owns two directories
what_happened: ci_merge parks any branch touching a directory outside KNOWN_DIRS as 'touches unknown territory (needs M-0 judgment)' and re-flags it every five minutes. Six branches -- s17-fleet-evidence-capture, v11-negative-control-census, v13-audit-the-published-surface, v14-standing-negative-control-probe, v15-census-sampling-frame, v17-pin-the-partial-verdict -- were held on that, and OPS-M had been silent 339 minutes. Two of them (v11, v15) were the 340-point negative-control census on which the monitor had already opened five work orders and questioned a number in the paper. The day-1 harvest's own README predicted exactly this for fleet-study ('fleet-study is not in ci_merge.KNOWN_DIRS, any branch touching it will be stopped as unknown territory'); W-1630 confirmed it from the other side at 21:35Z.
why_it_was_invisible: It was fully visible as a count -- 6 blocked branches -- but not as a cause. Only when the merge queue's flags were grouped by reason did 'the blocker is a role, not a tool' become readable, which is why the audit's own suggestion is that the flag detail be grouped by reason.
detected_by: W-1630 (from inside the blocked branch) and OPS-A, audit cycle 23
detection_latency: a whole night; 339 minutes of referee silence at the time of measurement
fix: 911ec8e admits fleet-study and verify-lab to KNOWN_DIRS and all six landed between 22:53 and 23:00Z. The structural fix the audit asked for -- 'absent more than N minutes, the monitor rules in the referee's place' -- was not made, so the door is still one only the referee can open. Same shape as the day-1 APP-*/RES-* claim latch.

title: Merge conflicts went 4 to 7 to 9 across the night purely because the queue was stopped, and the branch carrying the gate fix became a conflict with its own fix
what_happened: Every merge into master makes a long-parked branch a little more conflicted. Over one night the merge-conflict count walked 4 -> 7 -> 9 while the queue was blocked on other causes. s14-gates-for-all -- the branch whose whole purpose was to land the Git Bash gate fix -- was first held out by the very defect it fixed, and then, once that fix reached master by another path, became a duplicate of its own result and is now itself a merge conflict. Nine genuine conflicts were boarded as S24, clustered on the files two agents each edit half of (PARTNER_SYNC.md, spec.py, the STATUS files).
why_it_was_invisible: The blocked-branch total barely moved (21 -> 19) while its composition changed completely. A single number cannot show that a queue is trading a cheap blocker for an expensive one.
detected_by: OPS-A, audit cycles 22 and 23, by grouping the flag batch by reason
detection_latency: measured across the night as it happened
fix: Boarded as S24, unclaimed at the end of the window. New class: the cost is not a defect in any component, it is a function of how long the queue stayed stopped -- nothing in the existing vocabulary names a failure whose price accrues with delay.

title: Three swallowed-exception sites made the health certificate cleaner the more the code crashed
what_happened: theoria-arm/inner/plan.py `_tier_bfs` pruned successors on `except Exception: continue` and then announced 'the whole reachable set (N states) was enumerated'; theoria-arm/inner/certify.py `_ambiguity` skipped pairs on `except Exception: pass` while they stayed inside the claimed N x M denominator, then reported constraint 9 passed; a0-spike/pipeline/stages.py `mine` read any crash as the miner's designed NoSeparatingGuard verdict. The negative sample is exact: the control enumerates 3 states and reports unsat / exhaustive=True / crashes=0; the poisoned run enumerates 1 state and, before the fix, still reported unsat / exhaustive=True / 'the whole reachable set (1 states) was enumerated'. Two adjacent bugs: a sweep looping states[:400] while the sentence reported len(states), and a missing-exception default of `Exception` that filed every crash as a constraint-9 clash -- a positive claim about the world manufactured from a bug.
why_it_was_invisible: The bias is one-directional and toward comfort. Every swallowed crash removes work, and the sentences that describe the work were computed from what survived, so a crashier run produced a shorter, cleaner, more confident certificate.
detected_by: RES-3, working board item E14
detection_latency: unknown -- present in committed artifacts
fix: Crash counts are now booked, and any exhaustiveness / coverage / no-violation field must be false when the count is non-zero; `unsat` degrades to `unsat_unsound`. theoria-arm 51 -> 59 tests, a0-spike 44 -> 50.

title: E14's own fix carried E14's disease: the crash ledger was snapshotted per exit and the success exit was missed, so a search that crashed and then found a plan published count 0 and optimal true
what_happened: The adversarial review of E14 found that the new crash ledger was snapshotted at each exit point and the `sat` exit had been missed. A search that crashed and subsequently found a plan therefore published `count: 0` alongside `optimal: true` -- the ticket's own disease surviving inside the ticket's fix. Three further findings: `optimal: true` was left ungated though it is an exhaustiveness claim; `adapt.repair` stayed true under 12 injected crashes; and the audited claim denominator was widened 3 -> 13 after the reviewer pointed out that the original 3 was 'a choice, not a finding'. Nine corrections were applied and one declined in part; the review's own verdicts on the fix were recorded as REFUTED / PARTIALLY REFUTED rather than argued with.
why_it_was_invisible: A per-exit snapshot is correct at every exit it covers. Missing one exit produces no error anywhere -- it produces a zero, and zero is the value that means 'clean'.
detected_by: the E14 adversarial review pass
detection_latency: within the same run
fix: Corrected before delivery. New class: false_positive_fix_blinds_the_check is about a repair that disables a detector; this is a repair that reinstantiates the exact defect it was written to remove, and it happened twice in this window (see F-111).

title: Eleven engine-rig sites read a tool's failure as a fact about the world, and the canonical predicate for the worst one was imported and never called
what_happened: A survey of engine-rig for 'tool failure state (timeout / exit code / solver UNKNOWN / search exhausted / budget hit) converted into a boolean claim about the world' upheld all 11 sites it named. The sharpest: engine-rig/tools/p13_fd_dividend.py imported backends.proves_unsolvable and never called it, re-implementing it at line 129 as a bare `returncode == 12` that dropped both of the original's conditions. Others: two crashed FD runs recorded as `same_answer: True`; lp_potential collapsing an iteration limit into infeasibility; zero_space truncating past 8 colours and labelling the law `scope: global` (already discharging -- a 10-colour ARC palette triggers it); mdl_segmenter's IMPOSSIBLE sentinel becoming indistinguishable from 'nothing changed'; and a family of 5 subprocess call sites using text=True with no encoding=, destroying diagnostics exactly when they are needed.
why_it_was_invisible: Each site produces a well-typed boolean of the right shape. A canonical predicate that is imported but never called is invisible to an import-graph check and to a linter, and identical-looking to one that is used.
detected_by: RES-3's read-only cross-check survey, re-verified line by line by the engine-rig session working C11
detection_latency: unknown -- long-standing committed code
fix: 10 of 11 fixed (three-valued results, explicit exceptions, encoding pinned); site #9 declined with a written reason, then reclassified by the reviewer as an adjudication-layer defect rather than a rendering one and left in place marked OVERTURNED.

title: The C11 survey's own counts were wrong twice, and a table column labelled 'location in the current tree' actually held pre-fix locations
what_happened: The first pass reported '10 sites plus a family of 4, 9 fixed'. Adversarial review made it 11 sites plus a family of 5, 10 fixed: site #12 (deadlock_carver's same_answer, the same shape as the p13 defect) had been missed and had earlier been declined under a double standard, and the encoding family repaired 5 call sites while self-reporting 4. Separately the table's header column claimed to give current-tree locations and gave pre-fix ones -- the data was right, the label was not. All three are marked [OVERTURNED] in place rather than silently rewritten.
why_it_was_invisible: A count in a delivered report is the artifact a reader trusts instead of re-deriving. Nothing recomputes it, and a label on a correct column is the kind of error that survives proofreading.
detected_by: the C11 adversarial review
detection_latency: within the same run
fix: Booked in place with no defence, per the delivery's own stated rule.

title: One C11 repair was inert -- deleting it left 452 tests green -- and a mutant that made the new scanner return nothing also left the suite green
what_happened: The first repair of site #8 (probe_frontier) added basis/budget fields that never reached the payload, sat behind an unreachable else, and had no negative sample; the reviewer deleted the whole repair and 452 tests stayed green. Separately, the standing AST check shipped with the ticket had its scanning layer untested: mutant M35, replacing check_paths with `return []`, did not turn the suite red. And the delivered mutation figure '18/18 kills, 0 escapes' was false -- the reviewer ran 36 mutants and got 31 killed, 5 escaped (M25, M26, M28, M35, M36).
why_it_was_invisible: A test suite that never exercises the scanner cannot tell the scanner apart from a stub. The mutation score that would have shown this was itself computed on too small a mutant set, so the instrument meant to catch a missing failing path had a missing failing path.
detected_by: the C11 adversarial review
detection_latency: within the same run
fix: Site #8 rewritten to raise at the point of judgement with a negative sample; seeded-file scan tests added and runs/ removed from the skip table; the escaped mutants closed (9/9 red).

title: An optimistic dict default wrote 'I could not check this' as 'this holds' in 13 of 35 shipped ground-truth files, while the Markdown from the same call said 'unverified'
what_happened: worldgen/core/truth.py computed `"invariants_all_hold": all(i.get("holds", True) for i in invariants)`. A prose-only invariant has no `holds` key, so the default silently promoted unverified to verified, and worldgen/build.py then folded it into `invariant_failures: []` -- the list the build gate reads. 13 of 35 shipped ground_truth.json files asserted invariants_all_hold: true while GROUND_TRUTH.md, rendered from the same dict in the same call, printed 'prose only, unverified'. Only the machine-read half lied. A sweep found two more optimistic defaults of the same shape: gate_failures reading totals.get(key, ()) (a missing gate key silently clears the gate) and to_markdown's corr.get("agrees", True).
why_it_was_invisible: The human-readable artifact was honest, so any reader who checked by eye saw the truth; only the gate, which reads the JSON, saw the lie. A default argument is also the least conspicuous place in Python for a policy decision to live.
detected_by: the worldgen session working V19
detection_latency: unknown -- 13 shipped artifacts already carried it
fix: Three-class partition holds/violated/unverified with a separate invariant_unverified gate (deliberately not a one-character widening of invariant_failures); zero-state callables count as unverified. All 13 were then actually exercised via a new edge_check seam and came out true on 104-1744 measured transitions each. 512 -> 514 tests. NOT ON MASTER at the end of the window: 23ec179 is on agent/v19-unverified-is-not-true only.

title: The rig has never validated anything it did not fit: a repo-wide grep for held-out validation returns nothing, and zero_space.verify re-checks on the trajectory it was fitted to
what_happened: RES-3's fourth read-only survey found no held-out validation anywhere in engine-rig, while zero_space.verify re-checks its result against the same trajectory the result was fitted to -- which under a GF(2) construction is close to a tautology. The monitor's own wording: 'verified', in several cells of the engine table, currently means 'self-consistent on the data it was fitted to'. This is not a hedge about the paper's phrasing; it is what those cells mean today.
why_it_was_invisible: A verifier that re-runs on the fitting data passes, always, and passing is exactly what a verifier is supposed to do. Nothing in the artifact distinguishes 'checked against new data' from 'checked against the data that produced it'.
detected_by: RES-3's fourth survey, adjudicated by the monitor
detection_latency: unknown -- predates the eight engine-rig milestones
fix: Boarded as E17, unclaimed at the end of the window.

title: The verdict is computed, written into the artifact, and then not used as the gate -- a theorem and a report falsifying it get published side by side
what_happened: engine-rig/engines/lp_potential/potential.py:296 publishes `"admissible": True` as a literal while the actual admissibility test lives at line 320 in a sibling field of the same payload -- the answer and the check ride in the same dict and neither consults the other. engine-rig/engines/deadlock_carver runs carve, report and emit with no conditional between them, so a theorem and a report falsifying that theorem are emitted together with neither overruling the other.
why_it_was_invisible: Both the claim and its refutation are present in the artifact, so an auditor reading it can see the problem -- but no code path does, and the consumer takes the first field.
detected_by: RES-3's fourth survey, adjudicated by the monitor
detection_latency: unknown
fix: Boarded as E16, deliberately kept separate from E17 on the argument that an acceptance line nobody can re-check is not an acceptance line. Unclaimed at the end of the window.

title: release/checklist.py carries a committed syntax error: the encoding fix meant to stop mojibake was written with a literal newline inside the string
what_happened: release/checklist.py:45 reads `_stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="` followed by an actual line break and a closing quote -- the escape `\n` was written as the character it denotes. Both ast.parse and running the file raise SyntaxError: unterminated string literal. Independently confirmed here on the live tree. The comment above it explains that the pin exists because seven of ten item names had rendered as mojibake for a reader following REPRODUCING.md; the fix for that unreadability is itself unrunnable. Surfaced as one unparseable file among the 26 hits of C11's repo-wide AST scan.
why_it_was_invisible: Nothing in release/ runs it in CI, and a file that will not parse is silently skipped by every AST-based tool, including the scan that found it -- it appeared as a count of unparseable files, not as an error.
detected_by: C11's calibration scan, reported to the inbox as out of territory
detection_latency: unknown -- still broken in the worktree at the end of the window

title: A false red was masking a real one: when the gate defect cleared, e9's blocker changed from 'verify gate red in fuzzlab' to 'tests red in engine-rig' with three facts disagreeing with their artifacts
what_happened: monitor/ci/CONFLICT-origin_agent_e9-engine-paper-table.md was rewritten in c343976: reason `verify gate red in fuzzlab (verify.py)` became `tests red in engine-rig`. The real failure had been sitting behind the harness failure the whole time -- test_engine_table reports three facts disagreeing with their artifacts: rig.campaign_worlds artifact 60 vs table 500, rig.mutants 64 vs 55, rig.survivors 14 vs 15.
why_it_was_invisible: One red hides another. While the gate could not run, the branch's flag named a territory and a runner, and no one looked past it; only clearing the false red exposed which branches were genuinely failing.
detected_by: the merge queue, once gates ran for real
detection_latency: hours -- from the branch's first flag to 23:41Z
